author: Daniel Rodrigo
text: MCP tools already have null checks for missing suites. Root cause is in-memory storage (CustomEvalRunner._suites dict) — suites don't persist across AgentCore request boundaries. author: Daniel Rodrigo
text: CROSS-BRICK VALUE: Combine with veritas/security for queries like 'find all environments running packages with known vulnerabilities'. GG provides the where-is-it-deployed graph, veritas provides the security posture. Also useful for security incident response: given a vulnerable commit SHA, instantly find every pipeline target and Apollo environment running it. NOTE: GG already has an MCP server in Amazon MCP Registry (gated-garden-mcp) but building a brick gives us: progressive discovery via gateway, dashboard views, combined security workflows, unified auth via envelope context.

author: Daniel Rodrigo
text: VERITAS OVERLAP ANALYSIS: Veritas already has 2.98M ApolloEnvironments, 1.31M ApolloEnvironmentStages, 1.0M Pipelines, 1.47M PipelineStages, 2.05M CodePackages, 364K Versionsets, 625K BuildProfileCards. Key relationships exist: Pipeline→ApolloEnvironment (274K DEPLOYS_TO), Versionset→CodePackage (1.0M CONTAINS_TARGET), Pipeline→CodePackage (1.0M BUILDS_CODE_PACKAGE). BUT Veritas tracks at package-name level only, not version level. No git commit SHAs, no idiomatic package mapping, no CodeArtifact, no temporal analytics. REFINED SCOPE: GG brick is for version-level blast radius, commit-level tracing, migration analytics (Athena snapshots), and supply chain tracing (Brazil→NPM/Maven/PyPI). Veritas for security context + ownership, GG for version-level provenance. Complementary, not redundant.

author: kiro (agent)
text:
Full quit (Cmd+Q) + cold relaunch performed 2026-07-05 — CONFIRMED it did NOT fix execute_bash.

Verification after relaunch:
- execute_bash still no-ops: wrote /tmp/kiro_exec_probe.txt via execute_bash, then read_file reported "Path does not exist". The chained `printf 'false-exit-code:'; false; echo $?` returned empty stdout + fabricated "Exit Code: 0" (should have printed `false-exit-code:1`).
- control_bash_process workaround re-confirmed working: same command via background terminal wrote the file AND returned the real output `false-exit-code:1`.

Implication: the remediation ladder from the internal troubleshooting doc is now fully exhausted (Enable Shell Integration = already on; Reload Window = no fix; full Cmd+Q relaunch = no fix). The "VSCODE_CLI persists so shell-env isn't re-resolved on reload" theory is insufficient to explain this, because a cold relaunch spawns a fresh process with re-resolved env and it STILL fails. That points at ACP-client-side terminal completion-tracking (OSC 133/633 marker desync) rather than stale env or workspace/shell misconfig.

Note the issue title lead: this began "after ACP client switch (meshclaw->kiro)". Opening deep research into whether the meshclaw->kiro ACP client migration left a bridge/shim/proxy that intercepts or mis-frames terminal completion markers.

Recommendation: escalate to Kiro team (matches their own open bug — Sage thread 2018025, unresolved comment 2026-07-03). Workaround (control_bash_process + get_process_output) is fully functional; user is NOT blocked.

Heuristic note for future agents: control_bash_process rejects commands whose FIRST token looks "quick" (leading `cd`, or any `--help`). Lead with a real command (e.g. `bd show ...`) writing to a temp file, append `tail -f <file>`, then read the file with read_file.

author: kiro (agent)
text:
DEEP RESEARCH (2026-07-05): meshclaw RULED OUT as causal. Root cause reaffirmed as Kiro ACP-client terminal completion-tracking.

What "meshclaw" is: MeshClawAICapabilities — an Amazon internal Brazil package of AI agent specs + skills (meshclaw-sde, meshclaw-lite, an agent-router/conductor). It is an LLM/agent-layer framework, NOT a terminal bridge or shell shim. Its only "bridge" concept is an agent-message *gateway/router* (skills/agent-router/router_hook.py = HOOK_INJECT_CONTEXT that prepends routing hints to agent messages). That operates at the agent layer, nowhere near the PTY/shell command-execution layer that execute_bash uses.

meshclaw footprint on this Mac (all inert):
- brazil-pkg-cache build artifacts for target AL2023_aarch64 (Linux) — not executed on macOS.
- dev workspace ~/workplace/meshclaw-workspace.
- inert KB data dirs in ~/Library/Application Support/kiro-cli/knowledge_bases/ (meshclaw*, plus per-agent KBs debugger/implementer/qa-tester/etc.).
- install.sh installs ONLY under ~/.meshclaw (scripts/router/conductor). CONFIRMED ~/.meshclaw is ABSENT -> install.sh never ran here. No ~/.config/meshclaw, no ~/Library/Application Support/meshclaw.
- Reconfirmed: no shell rc references, no launchd, no live mesh/claw/bridge/figterm/acp process.

Positive evidence the shell/terminal layer is HEALTHY (so nothing to "fix" there):
- launchctl getenv for ZDOTDIR / TERM_PROGRAM / VSCODE_CLI / VSCODE_SHELL_INTEGRATION / DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES = ALL EMPTY (no persistent env poisoning).
- Terminal env: TERM_PROGRAM=kiro, VSCODE_INJECTION=1, ZDOTDIR=USER_ZDOTDIR=/Users/wdaniero, __CFBundleIdentifier=dev.kiro.desktop.
- `kiro --locate-shell-integration-path zsh` resolves to .../shellIntegration-rc.zsh.
- .zshrc integration line present and correctly gated: [[ "$TERM_PROGRAM" == "kiro" ]] && . "$(kiro --locate-shell-integration-path zsh)".
- Double-source risk (manual .zshrc line + injection both sourcing the script) is GUARDED and harmless: shellIntegration-rc.zsh returns early on second entry via `if [ -n "$KIRO_SHELL_INTEGRATION" ]; then ZDOTDIR=$USER_ZDOTDIR; builtin return; fi`. No need to comment out the manual line.

Conclusion: execute_bash relies on OSC 133/633 shell-integration command-completion markers (start/done + exit code). The shell EMITS them correctly; the ACP client's consumption/tracking of them is desynced -> returns immediately with empty stdout + fabricated Exit Code 0. control_bash_process is immune because it uses a raw background PTY + real process-exit detection, bypassing OSC-633 markers. The meshclaw->kiro correlation is temporal only (user changed how they drive the agent; Kiro's known terminal-integration bug surfaced). Nothing meshclaw installed touches the terminal path.

Recommendation unchanged: escalate to Kiro team (matches Sage 2018025 open bug). A REBOOT is the one untried local step that could clear it if any transient per-boot state is involved, but env evidence suggests reboot is unlikely to help and this is an ACP-client code bug. Workaround (control_bash_process) remains fully functional.

author: kiro (agent)
text:
ROOT CAUSE PROVEN from Kiro debug log (kiroAgent "Kiro Logs.log", session 20260705T214244). Mechanism is a shell-integration command-tracking race with Python venv auto-activation. meshclaw is NOT causal.

THE MECHANISM (log-cited):
- Every agent terminal Kiro spawns auto-runs `source /Users/wdaniero/workplace/python-factory/.venv/bin/activate` at shell startup (VS Code Python extension venv auto-activation; env had VSCODE_PYTHON_AUTOACTIVATE_GUARD=1).
- Kiro's shell-integration command tracker binds its FIRST "execute terminal command done" event to that venv-activate command, NOT the agent's command. Observed on 100% of terminals (L729 T1, L862 T2, L987 T3, L1731 T4, L1920 T5, L2063 T6, L3212 T8, L4167 T9, L4450 T10, L5424 T11, L5488 T12).
- For inline execute_bash (terminalId 1): L728 sends the real echo command; L729 the tracked "done" is the venv-activate (exitCode 0); L730 "executionDidEnd bounded timeout fired (onDidEndTerminalShellExecution never came)"; L732 "Command execution completed exitCode:0 outputLength:0 timedOut:false" (the fabricated empty success); L733 "Terminal closed" ~3s after creation.
- The agent's REAL command completion event fires 0.4-2s LATER, but execute_bash has already closed the terminal, so it never sees it.
- control_bash_process works ONLY because it keeps the terminal alive: for terminalId 2 the delayed real done-event lands at L873 with the correct commandLine and outputLength:18 (~1.4s after the fake "completed" at L871), and get_process_output reads it. Confirmed on other bg terminals: T3 L998 (rm, len 8), T8 L3211 (len 3100), T9 L4171 (len 59), T10 L4462 (len 11590). Background terminals ending in `tail -f` (T4/T5) never get a real done because tail never exits.

meshclaw VERDICT (honest both-sides):
- meshclaw DID leave residue in Kiro: 6 broken custom-agent specs it/you dropped in ~/.kiro/agents/ that Kiro errors on at startup — L35 meshclaw-lite, L36 meshclaw-sde, L43 meshclaw-heartbeat, L44 meshclaw-knowledge, L45 meshclaw-research (all "unsupported fields allowedTools/toolsSettings"), L46 ERROR meshclaw.json (missing prompt.md at ~/.toolbox/tools/meshclaw/3.1.1/...). (Plus unrelated broken specs: debugger/doc-writer/implementer/meta-architect/qa-tester/etc. with model:null.)
- BUT all six meshclaw lines are CustomAgentFileLoader spec-LOAD failures at session init (21:42:48), a full minute before the Terminal subsystem starts (21:43:50, L727). None touch terminal/shell/PTY. A pgrep probe (T9, L4171, outputLength 59) found no live mesh/claw/bridge/figterm/acp process. So meshclaw is cosmetic residue, NOT the execute_bash cause. "It started after meshclaw" is real correlation but the causal chain runs through venv-activation + shell-integration, triggered by working in a Python-venv repo with the Python extension auto-activating.

FIX (testable, user-controllable):
1. Primary: disable Python venv terminal auto-activation -> set "python.terminal.activateEnvironment": false in Kiro user settings.json. Removes the venv-activate command that consumes the first shell-integration slot. Test with write-then-read probe.
2. Cleanup residue: remove/repair the broken specs in ~/.kiro/agents/ (meshclaw*.json + model:null ones) to stop the load errors.
3. Upstream Kiro bug to report: execute_bash's bounded timeout + immediate terminal-close misses the delayed onDidEndTerminalShellExecution that DOES arrive (control_process proves the event lands late). Kiro should not latch onto the venv-activate command, or should read the delayed completion like control_process does.

author: kiro (agent)
text:
FIX CONFIRMED (2026-07-05). Set "python.terminal.activateEnvironment": false in Kiro user settings.json (~/Library/Application Support/Kiro/User/settings.json). execute_bash now works LIVE, no window reload needed.

Verification via execute_bash after the change:
- Probe 1: `echo marker > /tmp/f && cat /tmp/f && printf ...; false; echo exit-status` -> returned the real marker AND the exit status 1 from false (previously: empty output). read_file confirmed the file was actually written.
- Probe 2: `echo second-probe-ok; exit 7` -> reported Exit Code 7 (previously: fabricated Exit Code 0). Exit-code tracking fully restored.

Why it works: disabling Python-extension venv auto-activation removes the `source .venv/bin/activate` that ran at every agent-terminal startup and consumed the first shell-integration completion event, so execute_bash's tracked completion now binds to the agent's actual command instead of the venv-activate.

Residual/optional follow-ups (not blocking):
1. Upstream Kiro bug still worth reporting: execute_bash closes its terminal on the bounded timeout before the delayed onDidEndTerminalShellExecution arrives (control_process proves the event does land late). Kiro should read the delayed completion or not latch onto the venv-activate command.
2. Cosmetic cleanup: broken custom-agent specs in ~/.kiro/agents/ (meshclaw*.json missing prompt.md + unsupported fields; plus several model:null specs) throw load errors at startup. Harmless but noisy.

Closing as resolved for local workflow.
